findings.priority_reason: Changes to exception handling in input stream iteration modify runtime behavior when reading user input, replacing StopIteration with EOFError which may break existing error handling logic in user applications.
findings.title: Exception type change during input stream iteration
findings.before: The input stream iteration raised StopIteration when input was exhausted.
findings.after: The input stream iteration now raises EOFError when input is exhausted.
findings.scenario: A test runner calling the input stream's iterator until exhaustion.
findings.potential_impact: Applications catching StopIteration explicitly to detect end of input will no longer catch the exit condition, potentially leading to unhandled EOFError exceptions and crashes in test suites.
findings.review_question: Does the test suite rely on catching StopIteration when iterating over the simulated input stream?

example.input: A test runner calling the input stream's iterator until exhaustion.

analysis_limitations: Gemini inferred this example from selected excerpts. Reachability and downstream consequences are unverified.

findings.priority_reason: The input reading mechanism inside visible_input and hidden_input has transitioned from readline() to next(), fundamentally changing how input streams are consumed during CLI testing.
findings.title: Shift from readline to next for input stream consumption
findings.before: Input was consumed using the readline() method of the input stream.
findings.after: Input is consumed using the next() built-in, which triggers the new EOFError behavior upon exhaustion.
findings.scenario: A user invoking a command that requires multiple lines of input in a test environment.
findings.potential_impact: This change affects how custom input streams are handled, requiring them to be iterator-compatible. If an input stream implementation does not support the iterator protocol correctly, input consumption will fail.
findings.review_question: Are all custom input streams passed to the testing utility fully compatible with the iterator protocol?

example.precondition: A user invoking a command that requires multiple lines of input in a test environment.
